plan: My private value is $20. In a first-round auction with no prior history, the optimal strategy is to bid close to, but slightly below my true value. This minimizes overpaying while still having a good chance of winning. Since the third-highest bid determines payment, I'll bid $19.5 - this gives me a buffer and potential profit if I win, while not risking paying more than the item is worth to me.

My value is $29. In a second-price sealed bid auction, the dominant strategy is typically to bid your true value. Since I pay the third-highest bid, not my own, there's minimal risk in bidding close to my actual value. I'll bid slightly above my value to increase winning chances, but not so high that I risk negative profit. I'll bid $30 to give a small buffer above my true value.

My value is $45. In a first-price sealed bid auction with three bidders, the optimal strategy is to bid strategically below my true value. Since this is a single round with no repeated play, I'll bid close to my value but slightly below. This protects some potential profit margin. I'll bid $44.5, which is just under my true value, hoping to win while preserving some potential earnings if the third-highest bid is low.
